newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds consolidate, yields edge up.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds consolidate, yields edge up.

text.p: *Australian bonds yields edged up slightly during a more subdued session as the market consolidated after Thursday's buying spree on expections of an early interest rate cut.
*Market still pricing in a 50 basis point easing.
Australian bonds yields edged up slightly during a more subdued session on Friday as the market consolidated after Thursday's buying spree on expections of an early interest rate cut, traders said.

The 10-year bond yield crept back above 7.40 percent having dived to a 32-month low of around 7.38 percent on Thursday after this week's data showed benign growth in both inflation and wages, renewing hopes of a monetary policy easing.
And despite Friday's weaker tone, the market was still pricing in a 50 basis points easing by the end of the year.

Although the market will be avidly watching the Reserve Bank's daily dealing intentions for an indiction on policy over the course of the next week, as it did today, it is believed that if the central bank does ease it will be November 6.
This would be the day after the next board meeting.
A Reuters survey of economists gave a 60 percent chance of an easing by the end of November and a 75 percent chance by the end of the year.
Next week sees the release of the September balance of payments, building approvals and retail trade, none of which are expected to change the market's view policy expectations.

The local market gave up some ground against the U.S. bond market on the day, but the Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread remained well below the plus-100 basis points levels seen at the start of the week. Domestic bonds were also outperformed by New Zealand, but narrowed again against Canada.
The 10-year bond futures contract continued to hold support at 92.560, a level that had a stiff barrier on the market's recent advance.
